item.title: Katsurahama Beach and the Ryoma Statue — Guide
item.description: Katsurahama is one of Kochi’s most beloved beaches, a scenic crescent of sand backed by green pines and framed by rocky headlands where the Pacific rolls in. Long celebrated as a spot for moon-viewing, it is more a place for scenery than swimming — the waves and currents can be strong — and its great landmark is the towering bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma, the Kochi-born samurai visionary who helped bring about the Meiji Restoration and the birth of modern Japan.

item.title: Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum, Kochi — Guide
item.description: Sakamoto Ryoma is Kochi’s greatest hero: a low-ranking samurai from Tosa who became a visionary of the movement to overthrow the shogunate, broker alliances and open Japan to the modern world, only to be assassinated in Kyoto at just 31. This striking modern museum, perched on the headland above Katsurahama beach where his famous statue stands, tells his life and turbulent times through letters, artefacts and immersive displays, with dramatic ocean views from its galleries.
